about: Training lines for docs/experiments/natural_lines.md (experiments.py). Each line is one training history and has its own folder, runs/natural/<folder>/, with one subfolder per piece (train.py --resume adds pieces; --line <folder> starts a new line). This file gives each line folder a display id, name, purpose ('tested') and result ('found'), and notes on pieces (keyed by the piece folder name). Edit freely, then run experiments.py.

lines.name: no jump, constant LR
lines.tested: Can PPO learn to chop trees in a generated world at all? First natural-world run, the arena's 11 actions.
lines.found: Yes, but modestly: 9.7 logs per episode at 503k (random spawns), 5.3x random actions.

lines.name: jump, constant LR
lines.tested: Does adding jump and forward_jump help on hilly terrain? Compare with Line 1.
lines.found: Yes: jump nearly doubled the score at ~500k (18.0 vs Line 1's 9.7, random spawns). With a constant LR it peaked near 600k (18.1 on fixed spots) and then got worse: 15.0 at 1M, -3.1 +/- 2.6 logs vs its 601k checkpoint spot by spot.

lines.name: linear LR from Line 2's 601k checkpoint
lines.tested: Line 2 slid from ~22 to ~15 logs between 600k and 1M at a constant learning rate. Does decaying the rate to 0 keep the gains?
lines.found: Yes: from the same 601k model it rose to 24.7 on fixed spots, while Line 2 fell to 15.0. Spot by spot: +6.7 +/- 3.1 logs over the split point and +9.8 +/- 3.5 over Line 2 @ 1M. Best model so far.

lines.name: jump, linear LR, from scratch
lines.tested: Line 2b's recipe in one consistent setup from step 0 (3 instances, render distance 4, linear LR). Does the patchwork history of 2b matter?
lines.found: No: 22.4 on fixed spots at 1M, tied with Line 2b (-2.3 +/- 3.0 spot by spot), with fewer 0-log episodes (6 vs 13). So 2b's result doesn't depend on its patchwork history.

lines.name: fine-tune Line 3 @ 1.0M for 500k more at a small LR
lines.tested: Line 3 ended with its learning rate at 0. Does 500k more steps at a small rate (5e-5 -> 0) still improve it, or is it at its limit with this setup?
lines.found: No: 21.9 on fixed spots at 1.5M, -0.5 +/- 3.1 logs vs Line 3 @ 1.0M spot by spot (better at 41 spots, worse at 51). The extra 500k steps changed nothing measurable; with this setup the model looks to be at its limit.

lines.name: 3M linear LR schedule, from Line 3 @ 257k
lines.tested: Line 3's 1M schedule stalled near 22 and fine-tuning (3b) didn't help. Does one longer schedule (2.29e-4 -> 0 over 257k -> 3M, as if a single 3M run) keep improving past 22? Also the first run with 4 instances (same 2048-step updates).
lines.found: No: 23.9 on fixed spots at 3M, tied with Line 3 @ 1M (+1.5 +/- 3.4 spot by spot, better at 47, worse at 48) and Line 2b (-0.8 +/- 3.5). At 1M, with its rate still high, it was behind Line 3 (16.1, -6.2 +/- 3.6) and then climbed back to the same level. Every recipe so far ends at ~22-25, so the limit is the setup, not training length.

lines.name: multi actions (move x turn x look x jump, attack held), linear LR, from scratch
lines.tested: Every single-action recipe ends at ~22-25 logs, so the limit looks like the setup. Do multi-choice actions (choose move, turn, look and jump every step, attack always held, exact-degree turns) beat Line 3's 22.4 at 1M with the same schedule? In the fixed arena they scored 31.3 vs 30.5 (3 runs each, not significant: the arena is near its 32 cap).
lines.found: Yes: 26.6 on fixed spots at 1M, the best so far. Spot by spot +4.2 +/- 3.0 logs vs Line 3 @ 1M (same recipe, only the actions differ; better at 57 spots, worse at 36) and +1.9 +/- 3.4 vs Line 2b (not significant). It learned slower early (training avg 15.4 vs Line 3's 20.3 at 330k-423k) but kept improving after Line 3 levelled off (29.8 vs 25.5 at 900k-1M).

lines.name: resume Line 4 @ 1.0M for 1M more, linear LR from 1e-4
lines.tested: Line 4 was still improving at the end of its 1M schedule (training avg +4.6 logs in its last 100k), unlike Line 3, which had levelled off before 3b. Does 1M more steps (1e-4 -> 0) keep improving it?
lines.found: Yes: 35.7 on fixed spots at 2M, +9.1 +/- 3.6 logs vs Line 4 @ 1.0M spot by spot (better at 62, worse at 27). Held-out world 39.6 (gap +3.9, ranges overlap): it generalises. Training avg dipped for ~600k after the LR restart, then climbed as the rate fell.

lines.name: resume Line 4b @ 2.0M for 1M more, linear LR from 1e-4
lines.tested: Line 4b was still rising at 2M. Does a third 1M (same recipe) keep improving it?
lines.found: Yes, by less: 41.2 on fixed spots at 3M, +5.5 +/- 4.5 logs vs Line 4b @ 2.0M spot by spot (better at 54, worse at 38); 0-log spots 10 -> 7. Best model so far. A second 50-episode evaluation of the same model scored 40.5 (results/eval_results_natural_50ep_check.csv, kept out of the main table).

lines.name: wooded spawns, from Line 4c @ 3.0M, 1M more, linear LR from 1e-4
lines.tested: Line 4 does badly in snow and gets stuck. Do spawns in any biome with trees (snowy taiga, taiga, jungle, swamp, dark forest...; not savanna) and a new region every 5 episodes make the agent better in unfamiliar biomes, without losing forest skill? Same recipe as 4c's last 1M; Line 4d is the control (forest spawns).
lines.found: Yes, against its control (Line 4d: same 1M steps, forest spawns): wooded spots 31.6 vs 25.7, +6.0 +/- 4.8 logs spot by spot (better at 58, worse at 32); forest spots tied (40.0 vs 41.3, -1.3 +/- 5.0). 0-log episodes over both sets halved, 13 vs 26 (McNemar p = 0.007). Against its start, Line 4c, it is a tie on both sets (wooded +1.1 +/- 4.5, forest -1.2 +/- 4.7): the gain is that wooded spawns stopped the drop outside forests that more forest training causes.

lines.name: resume Line 4c @ 3.0M for 1M more, forest spawns, linear LR from 1e-4
lines.tested: Control for Line 5: the same 1M steps and recipe with forest spawns only, so Line 5's effect can be told apart from simply training longer.
lines.found: Forest score flat: 41.3 at 4M vs Line 4c's 41.2 (+0.1 +/- 4.5), so the line has levelled off. Wooded spots fell from 30.5 (4c) to 25.7: more forest-only training made it worse outside oak/birch forests. Line 5 (same steps, wooded spawns) beat it there by +6.0 +/- 4.8 and had half the 0-log episodes.

lines.name: wooded spawns from scratch, Line 4's recipe (multi actions, linear LR from 2.5e-4, 1M)
lines.tested: Line 5 showed wooded spawns help on top of a forest-trained agent. Does training on them from step 0 work as well, compared with Line 4 @ 1M (same recipe, forest spawns)?
lines.found: Stopped by hand at ~490k (not evaluated): its training average was behind Line 4's at the same point (about 10 vs 13-16 logs per episode around 400 episodes, ~400k steps, in), though wooded episodes are harder, so the two averages don't compare directly. Last checkpoint 480k.

lines.name: resume Line 5 @ 4.0M for 1M more, wooded spawns, linear LR from 1e-4
lines.tested: Line 4d showed forest training levels off by 3M. Wooded spawns give the agent harder places it hasn't mastered (31.6 wooded vs 40.0 forest), so does Line 5 keep improving with 1M more steps?
lines.found: No: wooded 31.3 vs Line 5's 31.6 (-0.3 +/- 4.5 spot by spot), forest 38.6 vs 40.0 (-1.4 +/- 4.5), both ties; 0-log spots 9 -> 7 wooded, 4 -> 6 forest. It keeps Line 5's lead over the forest-trained Line 4d on wooded spots (+5.7 +/- 4.7). Wooded training levels off by 4M too, so the remaining wooded-vs-forest gap (~8 logs) needs something other than more steps.

lines.name: resume Line 5 @ 4.0M for 1M more, spawns anywhere on land, linear LR from 1e-4
lines.tested: Wooded spawns halved the 0-log episodes (Line 5 vs Line 4d). Do spawns anywhere on land (plains, desert, savanna, mountains... where many spots have no tree in reach) teach the agent to search for trees and fail even less? Line 5b (same start, steps and LR, wooded spawns) is the control; scored on the oak/birch, wooded and new anywhere spot sets.
lines.found: No clear gain. Against its control Line 5b (same start, steps and LR, wooded spawns): anywhere spots 20.4 vs 21.1 (-0.7 +/- 4.5), oak/birch 36.6 vs 38.6 (-2.0 +/- 4.2), wooded 35.4 vs 31.3 (+4.0 +/- 4.7): all ties, the wooded one close. Against its start Line 5: wooded +3.7 +/- 3.5 (just significant), oak/birch -3.4 +/- 3.7, anywhere -1.1 +/- 4.3. 0-log episodes on the anywhere spots didn't move (Line 5c 36, Line 5b 37, Line 5 36); 28 of those spots are 0 for all three, probably no tree in reach. Trains as fast as wooded spawns (95 min for 1M).

lines.name: arena-pretrained start (multi actions + jump, 200k arena steps), then Line 4's natural setup for 1M (forest spawns, linear LR from 2.5e-4)
lines.tested: Does pretraining in the arena (9 minutes, 28.0 of 32 there) give a head start in the natural world? Same setup as Line 4; only the starting weights differ. Compared with Line 4 at equal natural steps. (Folder line6_...: named before Line 6, wooded spawns from scratch, was noticed; displayed as Line 7.)
lines.found: No lasting gain. Spot by spot vs Line 4 at the same natural steps: 260k -2.1 +/- 1.2 (10.7 vs 12.8), 500k +4.8 +/- 2.1 (17.8 vs 13.1), 1M -1.2 +/- 2.7 (25.4 vs 26.6, a tie). The head start (10.8 with no natural training) was gone by 260k while the agent unlearned arena habits. Step counts include the 200k arena steps (Line 7 @ 1.2M = 1M natural steps).
